paper.title_en: Nucleon spin structure from inclusive scattering
paper.abstract_en: The year 2025 marks the centennial of the discovery of spin. In this talk, I will first recount the story of the discovery based on a lecture given by Samuel Goudsmit himself. I then review recent results from Jefferson Lab on the nucleon spin structure functions in the very low $Q^2$, and then the very high $x$ region. The latter, often referred to as the deep-valence quark region, provides a clean testing ground of various predictions for the ratio of polarized to unpolarized structure functions, and quark polarization inside the nucleon. Preliminary results from the Jefferson Lab experiment E12-06-110 on the neutron spin asymmetry $A_1^n$ up to $x=0.75$ may start to challenge predictions from relativistic constituent-quark model, perturbative QCD, and holographic light-front QCD, even after accounting for the quark orbital angular momentum.
